cards.pattern: I'd like to ask for your help with something. Specifically, I need [type of help] with [specific task/problem]. This is important because [reason].
cards.quote: I'd like to ask for your help with something. Specifically, I need [type of help] with [specific task/problem]. This is important because [reason].
cards.zh: 有件事想請你幫忙。具體來說，我在［某件事］上需要你的［某種協助］。這件事之所以重要，是因為［原因］。
cards.why: 第一句先掛路牌，明說「接下來是一個請求」，對方就不用邊讀邊猜你要什麼。再把「要什麼」和「為什麼」拆成兩句，讓對方能分開評估。
swaps: Quick ask for you:
I need a hand with something—
cards.pmNote: 跨部門要資源時，signpost 讓對方知道這封信需要決定，不是 FYI。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: I'm asking you because [specific reason]. I'd need this by [date/time]. Is this something you're able to help with?
cards.quote: I'm asking you because [specific reason]. I'd need this by [date/time]. Is this something you're able to help with?
cards.zh: 我來問你，是因為［具體理由］。我需要在［時間］前拿到。這件事你有辦法幫忙嗎？
cards.why: 「為什麼是你」讓請求不像群發信。最後一句給對方一個能光明正大說不的出口（opt-out），反而提高答應率。
swaps: Is this something you have bandwidth for?
Would you be able to take this on?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: Our current [workload/situation] is unsustainable, and I'm causing [bottleneck] that will impact our ability to hit our targets.
cards.quote: Our current workload is unsustainable, and I'm causing bottlenecks that will impact our ability to hit our targets.
cards.zh: 我們現在的工作量撐不下去，而我正在造成瓶頸，這會影響我們達標的能力。
cards.why: 把「我做不完」翻譯成「公司會受影響」。書面請求要用對方在意的損失包裝，不是用自己的辛苦。
swaps: This is becoming a bottleneck for the whole team.
At the current pace we'll miss [target].
cards.pmNote: 對主管提資源需求時，痛點要落在團隊目標上，不能只落在個人負荷。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: You do this all the time at [scope], so I'd really like to share my existing [draft/plan] and have you pressure-test it based on your experience.
cards.quote: You do this all the time at the org level, so I'd really like to share my existing prioritization and have you pressure-test it based on your experience.
cards.zh: 你在組織層級天天在做這件事，所以我想把我現有的優先順序給你看，請你用你的經驗幫我壓力測試一下。
cards.why: pressure-test 把一個大請求縮成小請求：對方只要看你已經做好的東西，不必從零思考。同時抬舉了對方的專業。
swaps: I'd love you to poke holes in this.
Could you sanity-check my thinking here?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: Looking for a brain buddy on this—I have [N] questions. Are you open to answering inline or finding [N] minutes to chat live by [deadline]?
cards.quote: Looking for a brain buddy on this—I have 3 questions. Are you open to answering inline or finding 15 minutes to chat live by the end of this week?
cards.zh: 這件事想找個人一起想——我有三個問題。你想直接在訊息裡回，還是這週內抽十五分鐘聊一下？
cards.why: 先把請求量化（三個問題、十五分鐘），再給「打字回」或「講一下」兩個選項。量化＋二選一，是把「你有空嗎」變成好回答的最快方法。
swaps: I have 2 questions—happy to take them async.
Would inline replies work, or is a quick call easier?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: I don't want to make an avoidable error in how I'm thinking about [X].
cards.quote: I don't want to make an avoidable error in how I'm thinking about this.
cards.zh: 我不想在這件事的思考上犯一個本來可以避免的錯。
cards.why: 把求助動機說成「避免犯錯」而不是「我不會」，讀起來是謹慎，不是能力不足。書面上這個差別會被存檔。
swaps: I'd rather catch this now than after we ship.
I want to make sure I'm not missing something obvious.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.quote: I'm glad you want me to own this. I want to say yes, but I don't feel confident I can deliver it and need some support from you.
cards.zh: 很高興你想把這件事交給我。我想答應，但我沒把握能交出成果，需要你這邊的支援。
cards.why: 「我想答應，但」——先接住對方的期待再提條件，保住的信任比直接說「做不到」多得多。
swaps: I want to take this on, and here's what I'd need.
Happy to own it—with one condition.
cards.pmNote: 接下新專案時同步談資源，是 PM 少數能談條件的時機窗口。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: To do [existing goal] well and also take this on, I'd need us to either deprioritize [X] or staff up [Y] for success.
cards.quote: To do that well and also take this on, I'd need us to either deprioritize the other initiative or staff up the new project for success.
cards.zh: 要把那件事做好、同時又接下這件，我們得二選一：不是把另一個案子降優先，就是幫新案子加人。
cards.why: 不說「不行」，而是把條件寫成兩個具體選項讓對方挑。把決定權交回去，同時逼出一個真正的決定。
swaps: We can do this if we push [X] to next quarter.
Either [X] slips or we add headcount—your call.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: This conversation is meant to be an informal chat. I'd like to better understand your world and get your advice as I'm looking to [explain my goals].
cards.quote: This conversation is meant to be an informal chat. I'd like to better understand your world and get your advice as I'm looking to [explain my goals].
cards.zh: 這次就是隨意聊聊。我想多了解你們那邊的狀況、聽聽你的建議，因為我正想做［目標］。
cards.why: 明講「我不是來說服你的」，對方才敢給真情報。書面上尤其需要這句，因為沒有語氣可以傳達善意。
swaps: No agenda here—I'm just trying to understand how you see it.
I'm gathering context, not pitching anything yet.
cards.pmNote: 先蒐集 stakeholder 情報再提案，是 PM 影響力的第一步；情報階段千萬別讓對方覺得在被推銷。
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: I'm worried that [person X] might bring [argument Y]. Any chance you could chime in during the upcoming meeting or pre-brief [decision maker]?
cards.quote: I'm worried that [person X] might bring [argument Y]. Any chance you could chime in during the upcoming meeting or pre-brief [decision maker Y]?
cards.zh: 我擔心［某人］會提出［某個論點］。你有機會在會議上幫忙說一句，或先跟［決策者］通個氣嗎？
cards.why: 請人幫忙前先講清楚你怕什麼，對方才知道自己要補哪一塊。Any chance you could 是英文裡最不逼人的請求開場之一。
swaps: Would you be up for backing this in the meeting?
Could you give [decision maker] a heads-up beforehand?
cards.pmNote: 會議前先拉盟友（meeting before the meeting），比在會議上臨場辯贏有效得多。
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: Who are the two best [role]s you know? （取代 "Do you know anyone who..."）
cards.quote: Specifying "two best engineers" reduces the cognitive load put on the recipient and increases the chances that they send you a response.
cards.zh: 指名「兩位最強的工程師」降低了收信者的思考負擔，也提高了他回信的機率。
cards.why: 把開放式問題改成「講兩個就好」，對方的腦力成本從無限變成有限。限量是書面請求能不能拿到回覆的關鍵。
swaps: Who are the top two people you'd point me to?
If you had to name just one, who would it be?
cards.pmNote: 好的請求要 targeted、time-bounded、specific——執行成本壓到一分鐘以內，回覆率才會跳。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: Do you have a minute? （取代 "Sorry to bother you"）
cards.quote: Instead of: "Sorry to bother you." Say: "Do you have a minute?"
cards.zh: 不要寫「抱歉打擾你」，改寫「你有一分鐘嗎？」
cards.why: 台灣人寫英文信最愛開頭道歉。把「抱歉打擾」換成中性提問，請求的份量不變，但你不會先把自己降一階。
swaps: Got a minute?
When you have a moment—
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.pattern: Can you help me understand [X]? （取代 "Sorry, I didn't understand"）
cards.quote: Instead of: "Sorry, I didn't understand." Say: "Can you help me understand?"
cards.zh: 不要寫「抱歉，我沒聽懂」，改寫「可以幫我理解一下嗎？」
cards.why: 同樣一句「我沒懂」，寫成請對方協助就變成合作。書面道歉會被存檔、被轉發，主動語態才不會被讀成能力問題。
swaps: Help me understand the reasoning here.
Can you walk me through that part?
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.pattern: 刪掉 just / actually / quickly："I just wanted to ask..." → "I'm asking..."
cards.quote: "Just" demeans what you have to say. It shrinks your power and influence.
cards.zh: 「just」會貶低你要講的話，它會縮小你的份量與影響力。
cards.why: just、actually、quickly 這三個字是台灣人英文信裡最常見的自我縮小。刪掉之後句子不會變兇，只會變清楚。
swaps: I have a question. (不是 I have a quick question.)
I'd like to propose... (不是 I just think...)
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.pattern: Thank you for our conversation about [specific challenge they mentioned]. I've been thinking about your approach to [topic], and I wanted to share an insight from my experience with [relevant situation].
cards.quote: Thank you for our conversation about [specific challenge they mentioned]. I've been thinking about your approach to [topic], and I wanted to share an insight from my experience with [relevant situation].
cards.zh: 謝謝你上次談到［某個挑戰］。我一直在想你對［主題］的做法，想分享一個我在［類似情境］的心得。
cards.why: 追進度的信不要只寫「想跟進一下」。先還一點價值再開口，對方回信的動機就從人情變成划算。
swaps: Following up with something that might be useful:
One thought since we last spoke:
cards.pmNote: 面試後的 follow-up 附一個具體洞見（甚至小 prototype），比制式感謝信有效得多。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I'll keep you informed as I [continue the process]. Are you open to [specific action] on [day and time]?
cards.quote: I'll keep you informed as I speak with others on the team. Are you open to debriefing next Thursday after 2 p.m. PT?
cards.zh: 我跟團隊其他人談的進度也會同步給你。下週四下午兩點後方便一起回顧一下嗎？
cards.why: 收尾不寫「有空再回」，而是給一個指定時段，對方只要回 yes/no。同時暗示你這邊有進度在跑，不是在原地等。
swaps: Would Thursday after 2 work, or should I propose another slot?
I'll assume next Tuesday unless you say otherwise.
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I'll check back in [a week] or so—no need to answer right now.
cards.quote: In such cases, offer to check back in a week or so, giving them time to think about it.
cards.zh: 遇到這種狀況，就主動說一週後再來問一次，給對方時間想。
cards.why: 主動宣告「我一週後再問一次」，把追蹤變成事先講好的約定。第二次追就不會顯得是在催人。
swaps: No rush—I'll follow up next week.
Take your time; I'll ping you Friday.
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

cards.pattern: [What they did] helped me [concrete result]. Anything you need help with so I can return the favor?
cards.quote: Your backup with prioritization stuff helped me regain my sanity and actually figure out what work to do with my team. I feel a million times better, thank you for that! Anything you need help with so I can return the favor?
cards.zh: 你在優先順序上撐我那一把，讓我恢復理智、真的把團隊該做的事排出來了。我現在好太多了，謝謝你！有什麼我可以幫上忙的，讓我回報一下？
cards.why: 回報時要講出「後來發生了什麼」，對方才知道自己的時間沒白花。末句主動開一個互惠帳戶，比 thanks again 有力十倍。
swaps: Closing the loop: [outcome]. Thank you.
Let me know how I can return the favor.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: [Their answer] is helpful. I'm specifically looking for your help on [narrower ask].
cards.quote: The bigger org context is helpful. I'm specifically looking for your help on which of these three priorities I should drop this week.
cards.zh: 更大的組織脈絡很有幫助。不過我特別想請你幫的是：這三個優先順序裡，這週我該砍掉哪一個。
cards.why: 先肯定對方給的東西，再把問題收窄。等於不否定人地重新追同一件事——這是追第二次時最安全的寫法。
swaps: That helps. The piece I'm still stuck on is [X].
Useful context—my actual blocker is narrower: [X].
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.quote: Not an issue, I get it. Anyone else you would recommend I ask?
cards.zh: 沒問題，我懂。你會建議我再去問誰嗎？
cards.why: 被拒絕後不糾纏、改要一個轉介，把死路變成岔路。門留著，下次還敲得動。
swaps: Totally understand—any pointers on who else might know?
No problem. Is there someone better placed for this?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: After [the intro/help lands], send a note back to the person who connected you and tell them what came of it.
cards.quote: You should send a thank-you note to the person who made the connection to close the loop and let them know that their effort did not go to waste.
cards.zh: 你應該回一封感謝信給幫你牽線的人，把這個迴圈收起來，讓他知道他的力氣沒有白費。
cards.why: 追進度不只追人家欠你的，也包含回報結果。close the loop 是下次還請得動同一個人的原因，而幾乎沒有人做。
swaps: Closing the loop on the intro you made:
Wanted you to know how that turned out—
cards.pmNote: Sam 三年寄了 2,626 個請求給投資人，1,664 個有回覆——高回覆率來自每次都收尾。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.quote: "My heart says yes, but my schedule says no."
cards.zh: 我的心說好，但我的行事曆說不行。
cards.why: 把拒絕的責任推給行事曆而不是意願，對方不會覺得是自己不夠格。短到可以直接貼進 Slack。
swaps: I want to, but the calendar says otherwise.
Willing but not able right now.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: I thought carefully about this, as it's clearly a wonderful opportunity, but I'm going to decline with gratitude. I know [it] will be a big success!
cards.quote: I thought carefully about this, as it's clearly a wonderful opportunity, but I'm going to decline with gratitude. I know the book will be a big success!
cards.zh: 我認真考慮過了，這顯然是個很棒的機會，但我還是心懷感謝地婉拒。我相信這本書一定會大成功！
cards.why: 「我認真想過」讓拒絕不像反射動作。最後祝福對方成功，把關係從一次交易變成長期。
swaps: I gave this real thought before answering.
I'll be cheering this on from the sidelines.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: I'm running an experiment of not adding anything whatsoever to my to-do list right now.
cards.quote: I started an experiment of not adding anything whatsoever to my to do list so that it wouldn't get any longer.
cards.zh: 我開始做一個實驗：完全不再往待辦清單上加任何東西，免得它愈來愈長。
cards.why: 把「不」說成一個你正在做的實驗，聽起來是自我管理而不是嫌棄對方。實驗有期限，門也就沒有關死。
swaps: I'm not taking on anything new until [date].
I'm turning things down as a blanket policy at the moment.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: We must choose between [X, the new request] or [Y, an existing priority]. Should we do X or Y?
cards.quote: "We must choose between [X, new request] or [Y, existing item on OSR]. Should we do X or Y?"
cards.zh: 我們必須在［X，新需求］和［Y，現有優先項］之間選一個。要做 X 還是 Y？
cards.why: 書面拒絕的核心句：不是「做不到」而是「請你選」。把痛苦轉成一個對方有權做的決定。
swaps: Taking X means Y slips to next quarter. Which do you want?
This is an either/or, not an and.
cards.pmNote: 把決策寫在文件最上面（BLUF），再用 SCQA 展開，主管才會真的做選擇。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: 避免寫："We are thin on resources." / "I'm not sure if this is really high-priority."
cards.quote: It turns out that statements like these are counterproductive. They actually invite leadership teams to avoid the choice you're presenting.
cards.zh: 結果證明這類說法反而幫倒忙。它們等於在邀請主管迴避你提出的那個選擇。
cards.why: 模糊的訴苦（我們人不夠、我不確定這優先度高不高）給了主管理由叫你兩個都做。把話寫成一個明確的二選一，對方才必須真的選。
swaps: 換成："Doing X requires dropping Y."
換成："Here's the tradeoff, and here's my recommendation."
cards.pmNote: 說「資源很緊」是 PM 最常見的無效拒絕——它聽起來像抱怨，不像決策請求。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.quote: Can you tell me the salary band for this level? Happy to let you know if it's within my range, and we can discuss specific numbers later when I've met the team.
cards.zh: 可以告訴我這個職級的薪資帶嗎？我很樂意回覆你在不在我的範圍內，具體數字等我見過團隊之後再談。
cards.why: 被問期望薪資時反問級距，還附上一個「之後再談」的時間點——不回答但不失禮，是整場談判最關鍵的一句話。
swaps: What range is budgeted for this role?
I'd rather understand the band first before naming a number.
cards.pmNote: 談判從第一通 recruiter 電話就開始了；先報數字的人幾乎一定吃虧。
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.pattern: 收到 "give me your number and I'll make it happen" 時，不要回數字。
cards.quote: What recruiters say: "If you give me your number, I will make it happen for you." What they mean: "I'll get you something lower, but kinda close to what you asked for."
cards.zh: recruiter 會說：「你給我一個數字，我幫你搞定。」他真正的意思是：「我會給你一個低一點、但跟你要的差不多的數字。」
cards.why: 這句話幾乎每個 recruiter 都會寫。認得出來，你就不會把自己的底價先打進 email 裡。
swaps: I'd rather see the offer first.
Let's start from what the role is budgeted at.
cards.pmNote: 大公司薪資多由 compensation committee 決定，recruiter 未必有加碼權限。
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.pattern: I've received new information since we last spoke—[another offer / a counteroffer from my current team].
cards.quote: Most companies will consider "new information," like another offer, to reopen a negotiation. Don't forget, an offer to stay from your existing company also counts!
cards.zh: 多數公司會因為「新資訊」（例如另一個 offer）而重啟談判。別忘了，現職公司的留任提案也算數。
cards.why: 書面談薪要有「新資訊」才有正當理由重開談判。現職留任 offer 也算籌碼，是台灣人最常忽略的一張牌。
swaps: Something has changed on my end since we last spoke.
I've got a new data point I should share with you.
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.quote: Negotiating via email = MAJOR CRINGE and definitely a worse outcome. My advice if you want a meaningful/large increase is to have the conversation over the phone.
cards.zh: 用 email 談薪＝超級尷尬，而且結果一定比較差。想要有意義的大幅加碼，我建議直接電話談。
cards.why: 這組唯一一張叫你「別用寫的」的卡。email 談加薪拿不到大幅度；書面請只用來約時間、確認條款。
swaps: Could we find 20 minutes to talk this through live?
Easier to walk through on a call—when works?
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.pattern: 先談總額，下一輪再談單一項目：ask for "[total]" first, then "Can I have [X] more equity?"
cards.quote: Start with negotiating your overall compensation, not individual components. For example, ask for "500K" and then the next round ask "Can I have X more equity?"
cards.zh: 先談整體薪酬，不要一開始談個別項目。例如先要「50 萬」，下一輪再問「股票可以再多給 X 嗎？」
cards.why: 先總額再組成，順序反了就會被一項一項砍。簽字費放最後才拿出來要。
swaps: Let's align on the total package first.
Once we agree on the number, we can talk about the mix.
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.quote: I'm genuinely excited about this opportunity and can see myself making an impact. I'd love to discuss a few details to make sure we're aligned on expectations.
cards.zh: 我對這個機會真的很興奮，也能想像自己做出貢獻。我想討論幾個細節，確保我們對期待的認知一致。
cards.why: 談條件的標準開場：先把「我要來」講死，再說「有幾個細節」。熱情在前、議價在後，對方才不會以為你在猶豫。
swaps: I'm in—there are just a couple of things I'd like to align on.
Excited about this. A few details before we finalize:
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: What's the chance that we could explore a slightly different structure for [the compensation package]?
cards.quote: What's the chance that we could explore a slightly different structure for the compensation package?
cards.zh: 我們有多少機會可以試試看稍微不一樣的薪酬結構？
cards.why: 用機率問句代替要求。what's the chance 給了對方說「不高」的空間，反而讓他願意去幫你問。
swaps: Is there any flexibility on how this is structured?
How much room is there to reshape this?
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: I appreciate the strong offer. I'm wondering if we could find a way to bridge the gap between this and what would make it a complete win for both of us.
cards.zh: 謝謝你們給了很好的條件。我在想，我們能不能想辦法把這個數字和「雙方都完全滿意」之間的落差補起來。
cards.why: 先肯定 offer 再談落差，並用 for both of us 把加薪講成雙贏。書面談判最忌讓對方覺得你站在對立面，因為信會被轉發。
swaps: Can we close the gap between this and [number]?
What would it take to get us both to yes?
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: I'm thinking about how I can deliver the most value in this role. Would it make sense to discuss how the compensation structure could align with those key objectives?
cards.zh: 我一直在想我在這個職位上能交出最大的價值。要不要討論一下薪酬結構怎麼跟這些關鍵目標對齊？
cards.why: 把薪資綁在「我要交付什麼」上，談錢就變成談績效設計。這在書面往返裡特別有用，因為這封信會被轉給更多人看。
swaps: Could we tie part of this to the outcomes we just discussed?
I'd like comp to reflect the scope we've been talking about.
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: This looks promising, and I'm eager to move forward. Could we set up a quick call to discuss a few adjustments that might work better for everyone involved?
cards.zh: 這看起來很有希望，我也很想往下走。我們可以約個短會，聊幾個對大家都更合適的調整嗎？
cards.why: 「有進展＋想推進」再接「幾個調整」，保住動能的同時開了門。書面談判最怕沉默，這句把球丟回去但沒讓流程停下來。
swaps: Promising—can we grab 15 minutes to fine-tune a couple of things?
I'd like to move forward; a few adjustments first.
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: I want to be transparent—I have a few opportunities I'm considering right now. I'm most excited about our discussions and want to ensure we find the right fit for both.
cards.zh: 我想坦白說——我手上還有幾個機會在考慮。我最期待的是我們這邊的討論，也想確保這對雙方都是對的選擇。
cards.why: 講有別的機會但不威脅，還說最想來這裡。壓力來自事實而不是語氣——這是不撕破臉的施壓寫法。
swaps: Being upfront: I'm in conversations elsewhere too.
I'd rather be transparent about my timeline than play games.
cards.pmNote: Niya 說你不需要真的拿到多個 offer——能說「我正在跟其他公司談」就夠了。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I'm making a significant career decision and want to be thoughtful. I have a few conversations in progress. I expect to be ready to make a decision by [specific date].
cards.quote: I'm making a significant career decision and want to be thoughtful. I have a few conversations in progress, but I'm particularly excited about this opportunity. I expect to be ready to make a decision by [specific date].
cards.zh: 這是一個重大的職涯決定，我想想清楚。我手上還有幾個對話在進行，但我對這個機會特別有興趣。我預計在［日期］前能做決定。
cards.why: 自己訂決策日期，就不會被對方的限時 offer 綁架。主動給日期比拖延更顯得專業。
swaps: I'll have an answer for you by [date].
Does that timeline work with your hiring process?
cards.pmNote: Jacob 說收到 offer 後不到三到五個工作天就答應，通常代表你動作太快了。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I noticed the term "[vague term]" in our discussions. To ensure we're aligned, could you help me understand [the specific number] that represents?
cards.quote: I noticed the term "significant equity" in our discussions. To ensure we're aligned, could you help me understand the specific percentage or number of shares that represents?
cards.zh: 我注意到我們的討論裡出現了「可觀的股權」這個說法。為了確保雙方認知一致，可以請你說明那具體是多少百分比或幾股嗎？
cards.why: 把對方用的模糊字眼原句抄回去，再要一個具體定義。白紙黑字問過一次，之後就沒有「我以為」。
swaps: Can we put a number on "competitive package"?
What does "fully remote" mean concretely here?
cards.pmNote: significant equity、performance-based bonus、growth opportunity 這些詞每個人的解讀都不同，簽字前務必寫死。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I want to make sure I'm delivering exactly what you expect. When you say [vague term], what specifically would success look like in six months?
cards.quote: I want to make sure I'm delivering exactly what you expect. When you say [vague term], what specifically would success look like in six months?
cards.zh: 我想確保我交出的正是你期待的東西。你說的［某個詞］，六個月後具體長什麼樣子才叫成功？
cards.why: 用「我想做對」的姿態去逼出具體標準，聽起來是負責而不是不信任。六個月是很好用的期限錨點。
swaps: What metrics would tell us this worked?
How will we both know I've hit it?
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I read your [post] about [topic], and it sparked [a specific change] for me: [what you realized].
cards.quote: I read your post about saying "no" more, and it sparked a whole chain of events for me: I realized how much I've been people-pleasing, and it's exhausting.
cards.zh: 我讀了你那篇談「多說不」的文章，它在我身上引發了一連串反應：我發現自己一直在討好別人，而且非常累。
cards.why: 冷開場第一句必須證明你真的讀過、而且它改變了你什麼。「很喜歡你的文章」等於沒說。
swaps: Your talk on [X] changed how I run [Y].
I tried the [framework] from your post—here's what happened.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: I'm wrestling with one piece that I'm hoping you can help with: [one specific problem].
cards.quote: I'm wrestling with one piece that I'm hoping you can help with: I feel a profound guilt after I say no, and I ruminate on it for days after.
cards.zh: 有一個點我卡住了，希望你能幫上忙：我每次說不之後都會有強烈的罪惡感，還會反芻好幾天。
cards.why: 只問一件事，而且是對方寫過的題目的延伸。範圍越窄，陌生人越可能回。
swaps: One narrow question, if you have a moment:
The single thing I can't figure out is [X].
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: Do you have 1-2 tips you can share via email about [X]? Or I'd be happy to pay for a session if you're open to sharing your calendar link.
cards.quote: Do you have 1-2 tips you can share via email about how you navigate the aftermath? Or I'd be happy to pay for a session with you to talk more about it live if you're open to sharing your calendar link.
cards.zh: 你有沒有一兩個可以用 email 分享的心得，關於你怎麼處理事後那段？或者如果你願意給我行事曆連結，我也很樂意付費跟你聊一次。
cards.why: 給一個免費的小選項和一個付費的大選項，對方挑最省力的那個也是 yes。明講願意付錢，等於尊重了對方的時間。
swaps: Even a one-line answer would help—or I'm happy to book time.
Async is fine; a call is fine too, and I'd pay for it.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.quote: It's a trap to think you need to have some profound relationship first before asking. You can build the relationship while asking by making it significantly more compelling.
cards.zh: 以為一定要先有深厚關係才能開口，是個陷阱。你可以在開口的同時建立關係——只要把請求寫得夠有吸引力。
cards.why: 這句直接解掉台灣人「不熟不好意思問」的卡點。冷開場不是先套關係再開口，而是靠開口的品質建立關係。
swaps: We haven't met, so let me make this worth your time:
No relationship yet—here's why I think this is relevant to you.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.quote: My heuristic is simple: could my ask be at all compelling to this person?
cards.zh: 我的判準很簡單：我這個請求，對這個人來說到底有沒有一點吸引力？
cards.why: 寄出前的自檢問句。答不出來，就代表你還沒做完功課，那封信不該寄。
swaps: Why would this person care?
What's in it for them?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: 冷請求三原則：targeted（只寄給真的相關的人）／time-bounded（一分鐘內可完成）／specific（範圍寫死）。
cards.quote: Targeted: Only send them to the people who are relevant. Time-bounded: Ideally, executing the request should take less than a minute.
cards.zh: 精準：只寄給真的相關的人。有時限：理想上，執行這個請求應該花不到一分鐘。
cards.why: 陌生請求的回覆率不是靠文筆，是靠「執行成本」。把可完成時間壓到一分鐘以內，回覆率才會跳。
swaps: This should take you under a minute:
One reply-all-length answer is all I need.
cards.pmNote: 投資人不回信通常不是因為你用光了人情，而是因為你的請求寫得太難執行。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: In general, people like being helpful. By not asking for things, you're denying other people that joy.
cards.quote: In general, people like being helpful—especially investors! By not asking for things, you're denying other people that joy.
cards.zh: 一般來說，人是喜歡幫忙的——投資人尤其如此！你不開口，等於剝奪了別人得到那份快樂的機會。
cards.why: 重寫冷開場心態的一句話。不寄信不是客氣，是把對方幫忙的機會也拿走了——這個角度能直接降低開口的心理成本。
swaps: I'd rather ask than assume you're too busy.
Saying no is completely fine—I'd still rather ask.
cards.pmNote: 「人情籌碼有限」是錯覺；請求品質才是限制條件。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: In this post, I'll walk through [X] and show you how to use it as [用途] when [情境].
cards.quote: In this post, I'll walk through the model and show you how to use it as a practical diagnostic tool when a team is underperforming.
cards.zh: 這篇文章我會把這個模型走一遍，並示範團隊表現不佳時該怎麼把它當成實用的診斷工具。
cards.why: 先講「我會做什麼」再講「你能拿它幹嘛」，讀者兩秒內就知道要不要往下讀。關鍵在 as a practical diagnostic tool when...——它把抽象內容綁到一個具體使用時機上，讀者會自動對號入座。
swaps: In this doc, I'll lay out [X] and how to apply it when [情境].
This memo walks through [X] and how we'd use it in [情境].
cards.pmNote: 文件開場的職責不是介紹，是幫讀者做「要不要花時間」的決策。
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: In this [文件], I'll show you how to [目標]. You'll learn about [N] [問題類型] that silently break [你在乎的東西].
cards.quote: In this post, I'll show you how to get relevant and verified insights you can trust. You'll learn about four failure modes that silently break your AI-supported insights.
cards.zh: 這篇我會示範怎麼拿到你信得過、經過驗證的洞察。你會學到四種會悄悄毀掉 AI 分析結果的失敗模式。
cards.why: silently break 這個動詞組是重點：它暗示「你現在正在踩雷但不知道」，製造出讀者非讀不可的缺口。純寫 four common mistakes 就沒有這股拉力。
swaps: You'll learn the [N] [問題] that quietly derail [X].
I'll walk through [N] [問題] most teams miss.
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.quote: You think from the bottom up, but you present from the top-down.
cards.zh: 思考是由下往上，報告卻要由上往下。
cards.why: 一句話講完整個金字塔原則，而且是用對比句型（bottom up / top-down）把兩件事釘在一起，好記到可以直接在 review 會議上引用。台灣人寫文件最常犯的就是照著自己的推導順序寫。
swaps: Lead with the conclusion, not the journey.
Give away the punchline.
cards.pmNote: Minto 金字塔：先講結論 → 幾個支撐論點 → 每個論點配數據。
cards.episode: The Minto Pyramid Principle and the SCR Framework

cards.quote: As part of writing the document, I always put the decision right at the top—the "bottom line up front" (BLUF).
cards.zh: 寫這份文件時，我一定把決定放在最上面——也就是所謂的 BLUF（結論先行）。
cards.why: 破折號後面補一個業界通用縮寫，等於順手教了讀者一個詞、也標示你懂行規。在跨國團隊寫文件時，用對方圈內的術語會直接提高被當一回事的程度。
swaps: Decision up front, context below.
TL;DR at the top; supporting detail follows.
cards.pmNote: BLUF = bottom line up front，源自美軍公文寫作，矽谷文件普遍沿用。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: In this [文件], I'll walk you through [產出1]; [產出2]; and [產出3].
cards.quote: In this post, I'll walk you through three ways to create component libraries that consistently create great mocks; team workflows to reduce rework; and a step-by-step guide on how prototypes should be used.
cards.zh: 這篇我會帶你走過三件事：怎麼建出能穩定產出好 mock 的元件庫；怎麼設計團隊流程來減少重工；以及一份原型該怎麼用的逐步指南。
cards.why: 三個產出各自帶子句，所以改用分號而不是逗號分隔——這是英文文件裡處理「長項目清單」的正規做法，用逗號會糊成一團。
swaps: This doc covers [A]; [B]; and [C].
Three parts below: [A], [B], and [C].
cards.episode: How to get your entire team prototyping with AI

cards.pattern: The problem isn't that [表面診斷]; it's that [真正診斷].
cards.quote: The problem isn't that they lack ideas; it's that they try to prioritize fundamentally different kinds of systems as if they were the same thing.
cards.zh: 問題不在於他們沒有點子，而在於他們把本質上不同的系統當成同一種東西來排優先順序。
cards.why: 先否定讀者腦中最現成的解釋，再塞進真正的診斷——這個順序會讓讀者覺得「你比我想得深」而不是「你在教我」。分號比句號更能把兩半綁成同一個判斷。
swaps: It's not that [X]; it's that [Y].
The issue isn't [X]. It's [Y].
cards.episode: Not all AI agents are created equal

cards.pattern: Before you can decide [大決定], you need to answer a more basic question: [更基本的問題]?
cards.quote: Before you can decide which agent to build first, you need to answer a more basic question: What type of agent is each idea actually proposing?
cards.zh: 在決定先做哪個 agent 之前，你得先回答一個更基本的問題：每個點子提出的到底是哪一種 agent？
cards.why: 把讀者原本急著回答的問題往後推一格，等於重新設定整份文件的議程，而且不需要否定任何人。冒號後面直接甩出那個問題，讀者會不自覺開始在腦中回答。
swaps: Before we pick [方案], we need to agree on [前提].
The prior question is [X].
cards.episode: Not all AI agents are created equal

cards.pattern: [歸咎人] for problems that are actually [結構性的] is one of the biggest [領域] traps there is.
cards.quote: Blaming people for problems that are actually structural is one of the biggest leadership traps there is.
cards.zh: 把其實是結構性的問題怪到人頭上，是領導者最大的陷阱之一。
cards.why: one of the biggest ... traps there is 是英文裡把主張講重但不封死的固定說法（沒說「最大」，但氣勢等同）。用 trap 而不是 mistake，暗示這是誰都會踩的坑，讀者比較不會對號入座。
swaps: Treating [結構問題] as a people problem is one of the easiest traps to fall into.
It's tempting to read this as [人的問題]—I think it's [結構問題].
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: These mistakes are invisible until [後果 A], or [後果 B].
cards.quote: These mistakes are invisible until a stakeholder asks a question you can't answer, or a decision falls apart three months later.
cards.zh: 這些錯誤是看不見的，直到某個利害關係人問了你答不出來的問題，或某個決策在三個月後垮掉。
cards.why: invisible until 把「還沒發生的痛」寫成已經在倒數的東西，比 could cause problems 有壓迫感得多。兩個後果一個是當場丟臉、一個是延遲爆炸，覆蓋了讀者兩種恐懼。
swaps: This won't show up until [後果].
The cost is invisible now and expensive later: [後果].
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: Here's the problem: if you [做了 X] and then don't [做 Y], you're actually [更糟的結果] than if you had never [做 X] at all.
cards.quote: Here's the problem: if you ask someone to give you their precious time and feedback and then don't act on it, you're actually burning more trust than if you had never asked at all.
cards.zh: 問題在這裡：如果你請人花寶貴時間給你回饋，卻不採取行動，你其實比從來沒問過還更傷信任。
cards.why: Here's the problem: 是英文文件裡把讀者注意力硬拉回來的信號詞。後半的 more X than if you had never...at all 是反直覺結構，證明「什麼都不做」有時反而比較好，說服力很強。
swaps: Here's the catch: [反直覺後果].
Doing this halfway is worse than not doing it: [原因].
cards.episode: What 5 years at Reddit taught us about building for a highly opinionated user base

cards.pattern: We realized that the root cause of nearly all [問題類別] is very simple: [根本原因].
cards.quote: We realized that the root cause of nearly all bad planning processes is very simple: a basic lack of understanding of roles — who is responsible for what, when.
cards.zh: 我們發現幾乎所有糟糕的規劃流程，根本原因都很簡單：大家對角色沒有基本共識——誰在什麼時候該負責什麼。
cards.why: is very simple: 這個冒號前的鋪陳製造了一秒懸念，讀者一定會讀冒號後面。破折號再把抽象名詞翻成白話（who is responsible for what, when），確保沒有人誤解。
swaps: The root cause turns out to be simple: [原因].
Underneath all of these is one thing: [原因].
cards.episode: The Secret to a Great Planning Process — Lessons from Airbnb and Eventbrite

cards.pattern: We had established [A], [B], and [C], but [對象] were still confused about why [D].
cards.quote: We had established our product roadmap and success metrics and our mission and vision, but teams were still confused about why we were working on the projects we chose.
cards.zh: 我們的產品路線圖、成功指標、使命和願景都定好了，但團隊還是搞不懂我們為什麼在做這些專案。
cards.why: 先把「我們該做的都做了」列出來再說 but，讀者才不會以為問題出在偷懶。這是提出新提案前最有用的鋪陳：證明現有工具不夠，而不是沒人用。
swaps: We already have [A] and [B], and yet [問題] persists.
This isn't for lack of [既有努力]—[問題] still happens.
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: Every [角色] obsesses over [顯眼的東西], yet almost no one masters [真正的槓桿]: [X].
cards.quote: Every PM building with generative AI obsesses over crafting better prompts and using the latest LLM, yet almost no one masters the hidden lever behind every exceptional AI product: evaluations.
cards.zh: 每個做生成式 AI 的 PM 都在鑽研怎麼寫更好的 prompt、用最新的模型，卻幾乎沒人練成每個頂尖 AI 產品背後那個隱形槓桿：evals。
cards.why: everyone does X, yet almost no one does Y 是「機會缺口」的萬用句型，同時暗示讀者現在站在多數人那邊（不舒服）而你要帶他去少數人那邊。冒號留到最後才揭曉主題，張力拉滿。
swaps: Everyone is optimizing [X]; almost nobody is touching [Y].
The attention is all on [X]. The leverage is in [Y].
cards.episode: Beyond vibe checks: A PM’s complete guide to evals

cards.pattern: In this [文件], I won't cover [排除的東西], though they're [承認其重要性]. Instead, I want to cover [真正的範圍].
cards.quote: In this post, I won't cover traditional health tips (exercise, get eight hours of sleep, etc.), though they're crucial. Instead, I want to cover some of the lesser-known health gotchas that consistently sap your health.
cards.zh: 這篇我不會談傳統的健康建議（運動、睡滿八小時之類），雖然那些很重要。我想談的是那些比較少人提、卻持續在耗損你健康的細節。
cards.why: 先排除、再加一句 though they're crucial 承認被排除的東西有價值，讀者就不會覺得你在偷懶或無知。這個「排除＋致敬＋改談」三拍是寫 non-goals 最安全的句型。
swaps: I'm not covering [X] here—not because it doesn't matter, but because [理由].
Out of scope for this doc: [X]. In scope: [Y].
cards.episode: A builder’s guide to living a long and healthy life

cards.pattern: Below, I will focus on [A], [B], and [C]. The fourth, [D], is an equally valid focus area, but not one I'd suggest starting with, due to [理由].
cards.quote: The fourth, retention/expansion, is an equally valid focus area, but not one I'd suggest starting with, due to the complexity and effort required to improve those metrics.
cards.zh: 第四項——留存與擴張——同樣是合理的著力點，只是我不建議從它開始，因為要改善這些指標的複雜度和投入都太高。
cards.why: an equally valid ... but not one I'd suggest starting with 是排除選項時最有風度的講法：不貶低它，只講排序理由。due to 後面給出可檢驗的原因，別人要反對就得反對那個原因，而不是反對你的判斷。
swaps: [D] is worth doing—just not first, because [理由].
We're deferring [D] to [時間點] for [理由], not because it's unimportant.
cards.episode: Five steps to starting your product-led growth motion

cards.quote: Several areas that should explicitly *not* be the focus
cards.zh: 幾個明確「不」列為重點的領域。
cards.why: explicitly not 這兩個字是策略文件的分水嶺——沒寫下來的排除等於沒排除。放進「一份好策略包含什麼」的清單裡，等於把非目標升格成必填欄位。
swaps: Explicitly out of scope: [X], [Y].
Areas we are deliberately not investing in this cycle.
cards.pmNote: 好策略必含三塊：3–5 個重點領域、明確不做的領域、以及為什麼這樣選。
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: [X] exists to force a disciplined choice to deploy scarce resources for maximum impact.
cards.quote: Strategy exists to force a disciplined choice to deploy scarce resources for maximum impact.
cards.zh: 策略存在的目的，就是逼出一個有紀律的選擇：把稀缺資源投到影響力最大的地方。
cards.why: exists to 這個說法把一份文件的存在理由講死，適合放在目標段落最前面當定調句。force a disciplined choice 直接暗示「這份文件會讓人不舒服」，先幫讀者做好心理準備。
swaps: The point of this doc is to force one choice, not to list options.
This exists to make a tradeoff explicit.
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: To be clear, I'm not saying don't [做 X]. I'm saying [更精確的立場].
cards.quote: To be clear, I'm not saying *don't* do freemium. I'm saying it's a scalpel, not a sledgehammer, that requires thought.
cards.zh: 先講清楚：我不是說不要做免費增值。我是說它是手術刀不是大鎚，得動腦。
cards.why: To be clear, I'm not saying X. I'm saying Y. 是書面英文防誤讀的標配——文件會被轉發，你沒機會現場補充，只能自己先把可能的誤讀堵死。台灣人幾乎不寫這種句子，結果常被斷章取義。
swaps: To be clear, this isn't a case against [X]—it's a case for [Y].
I'm not arguing we stop [X]. I'm arguing we [Y].
cards.episode: Freemium vs. trial

cards.pattern: This should feel like common knowledge already, but remember, [重複的價值].
cards.quote: This should feel like common knowledge already, but remember, repetition doesn't spoil the prayer!
cards.zh: 這些你應該早就知道了，但別忘了——重複並不會壞了那句禱詞。
cards.why: 重述背景時最尷尬的是怕讀者覺得被當白痴，這句先承認「你早就知道」再給重述一個正當理由，尷尬就消失了。寫給高層的文件幾乎每份都需要這一句。
swaps: Most of this will be familiar—including it so we're working from the same page.
Recapping briefly for anyone joining this thread late.
cards.pmNote: 對高層重複priorities 不是囉唆，是讓你的優先順序在他們腦中有份量。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: The more work your team has done up front to [鋪陳], the less work your team will have to do when [壓力來臨].
cards.quote: The more work that your team has done up front to bring leadership into the story of your priorities and strategy prior to this decision point, the less work your team will have to do when new requests come in.
cards.zh: 你的團隊越早把主管拉進優先順序與策略的敘事裡，等新需求進來時要花的力氣就越少。
cards.why: the more... the less... 把「事前溝通」寫成一筆划算的投資而不是額外工作。bring leadership into the story 這個說法比 inform leadership 高明——它把對方變成故事裡的人。
swaps: The earlier we align on [X], the cheaper the tradeoff conversation gets later.
Front-loading this context saves us the argument in [時間點].
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: Over the past [N] years, I've used [X] in [N] different high-stake contexts, at companies large and small.
cards.quote: Over the past 10 years, I've used Strategy Blocks in six different high-stake contexts, at companies large and small.
cards.zh: 過去十年，我在六個高風險情境、大小公司都用過 Strategy Blocks。
cards.why: 用「年數＋次數＋公司規模跨度」三個數字建立可信度，比 I have a lot of experience with this 有力太多。high-stake 一詞暗示這不是紙上談兵。
swaps: We've run this [N] times across [情境], including [例子].
This is the [N]th time I've done this at [規模].
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: There's a moment most [讀者身分] recognize.
cards.quote: There's a moment most leaders recognize.
cards.zh: 有一個時刻，大多數領導者都認得。
cards.why: 六個字就把讀者放進一個共同經驗裡，而且製造懸念（是哪個時刻？）逼他讀下一句。開場不必先解釋背景，先讓讀者認出自己。
swaps: If you've ever [情境], you know the feeling.
Most of us have been in this situation: [情境].
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: After years of [做某事], I've noticed something surprising: [觀察].
cards.quote: After years of building AI products, I've noticed something surprising:
cards.zh: 做了這麼多年 AI 產品之後，我注意到一件出乎意料的事：
cards.why: 資歷（After years of）＋反直覺承諾（something surprising）＋冒號，三個元素合起來讓讀者非讀下一句不可。這是把個人背景轉成閱讀動力最短的寫法。
swaps: After [N] cycles of [X], one thing keeps showing up: [觀察].
Something we didn't expect kept happening: [觀察].
cards.episode: Beyond vibe checks: A PM’s complete guide to evals

cards.pattern: Everyone's [做某事]. But everyone's also getting [壞結果]: [具體症狀1], [症狀2], and [症狀3].
cards.quote: Everyone's "analyzing" customer data with AI. But everyone's also getting answers full of slop: hallucinations, wrong conclusions, and "insights" that just parrot back what you already told it.
cards.zh: 大家都在用 AI「分析」客戶資料。但大家拿到的也都是一堆垃圾：幻覺、錯誤結論，還有只是把你剛餵進去的東西再吐一遍的「洞察」。
cards.why: Everyone's X. But everyone's also Y. 用同一個句型重複兩次，第二次翻轉，節奏本身就在做論證。"analyzing" 的引號是書面英文的反諷手段——沒有語氣時，引號就是你的白眼。
swaps: Everyone is shipping [X]. Almost nobody is checking [Y].
We've all adopted [X]. What we haven't dealt with is [Y].
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: We've both been there, over and over again, while [具體經歷].
cards.quote: We (Tal and Aman) have both been there, over and over again while building AI products for tens of thousands of customers.
cards.zh: 我們（Tal 和 Aman）都經歷過，而且一而再再而三，就在替數萬名客戶打造 AI 產品的過程中。
cards.why: 先站到讀者同一邊（been there）再亮資歷，順序反過來就變成炫耀。over and over again 讓「我也犯過」聽起來誠實而不是客套。
swaps: We've made this mistake ourselves, more than once, while [經歷].
This isn't hypothetical for us—we hit it during [專案].
cards.episode: How to build AI product sense

cards.pattern: (To be clear, [避免誤讀的澄清].)
cards.quote: (To be clear, these layers are metaphorical and don't correspond exactly to org structure.)
cards.zh: （先講清楚，這些層級是比喻，並不完全對應到組織架構。）
cards.why: 整句放進括號，等於在正文旁邊加一條註腳而不打斷敘事節奏。文件會被轉發給沒上下文的人，這種當場拆彈的括號能省掉之後一整串誤會。
swaps: (Note: [澄清]—this is not a proposal to [誤讀].)
(For the avoidance of doubt: [澄清].)
cards.episode: How Notion builds product
